facts.fact: The Bank of the Republic of Burundi pilots BurundiPay, the national instant payment system, with 17 institutions live on 4 August 2026 (BRB payment systems director Nduwimana Libere).
The BRB has acceded to PAPSS and four Burundian banks are authorised to take part, according to BRB's Nduwimana Libere.

systems.owner: Bank of the Republic of Burundi

BDI.note: The fine is for banks missing the integration deadline, not a user-protection rule.

facts.fact: EAC central bank governors meeting in Kampala in July 2026 decided BurundiPay must be interconnected with other member states' payment systems for cross-border payments.
The BRB has acceded to PAPSS, with four Burundian banks authorised to take part, says BRB's Nduwimana Libere.

BDI.note: Nothing on government payments to people.
User and volume counts are not a survey share of adults.

facts.fact: BurundiPay, the national instant payment system run by the BRB, had about 224,000 users and about BIF 4.29 billion in cumulative transactions on 4 August 2026, with customers paying from bank accounts or e-wallets.

On BurundiPay 17 institutions (5 commercial banks, 10 microfinance institutions, 2 payment institutions) are live, and customers can transfer money and pay instantly from bank accounts or e-wallets, per the BRB.
BurundiPay is described as the national instant payment system run by the BRB, live since 5 March 2026 and launched publicly on 23 April 2026.

systems.owner: Bank of the Republic of Burundi
